officialIndustrialIdentity.finding: Eidsvoll Jernverk was established in 1624 as an industrial complex at Andelva. The watercourse supplied power for refining, hammers, sawmill, rolling mill and mill functions, while Eidsvollsbygningen served as the owner's residence within the wider works landscape.

survivingIndustrialEvidence.finding: Krutthuset is identified as the only surviving building from the old Eidsvold Jernværk. It is a rare timber powder house, probably dating from the seventeenth century.

historicalLandscapeContext.sourceName: Eidsvoll 1814 – Eidsvoll Verk as an industrial complex
historicalLandscapeContext.finding: The historical works included more than thirty utility and residential buildings, including smithies, hammer buildings, charcoal stores, sheds and the blast furnace. Surviving traces include Eidsvollsbygningen, a pavilion, Krutthuset and slag heaps.

mainAnchor.name: Vannkraft – ren energi
mainAnchor.finding: The named interpretation point sits in the immediate former ironworks and water-power core, close to Krutthuset and the main building but with a distinct industrial and hydrological subject.

secondaryAnchor.name: Langs Andelva
secondaryAnchor.finding: The named Andelva interpretation point extends the record eastward from the former works core into the industrial river corridor.

localityCrossCheck.name: Eidsvoll Verk
localityCrossCheck.finding: The village point confirms locality identity but is too broad to represent the historical ironworks and Andelva landscape.

separationFromBuilding.name: Eidsvollsbygningen
separationFromBuilding.finding: The adjacent building has its own canonical record and must not be reused as the industrial-landscape marker.

radiusDecision.reason: A 360-metre radius reaches the secondary Langs Andelva anchor approximately 331.1 metres from the main interpretation point while retaining a compact central industrial-landscape scope.

decision.representationLimit: The marker and radius represent the central interpreted ironworks and water-power landscape. They are not a legal heritage boundary, the full 15.5-kilometre Andelva corridor, the village centre or Eidsvollsbygningen itself.
